summary: Intermittent 401s: client cert CN with percent-encoding breaks token-exchange RBAC lookup in private deployment
description: Issue summary: After a planned IdP rotation and client cert reissue at FinServCo, a subset of API calls from the customer's private deployment started returning 401 Unauthorized during the token-exchange / client-identity mapping step. This appears intermittent and correlated with requests from a small fleet of service processes.
impact: Multiple internal services for FinServCo are failing auth checks intermittently; customer reports production impact for a small percentage (~5%) of requests that perform mTLS-backed token exchange. Immediate business impact: degraded processing of real-time transactions; not a full outage but causes retry storms and elevated latency.
environment_details: Private control plane with customer-managed ingress; auth-proxy runs as sidecar in their VPC. Customer-issued client certificates use a CN containing encoded characters (examples observed: 'svc%20team@corp' and 'svc%2Fpayments@corp'). Certificates were recently reissued as part of IdP automation.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use a client cert with a CN that contains percent-encoded characters (e.g., 'svc%20team@corp').
2) Make a call that triggers mTLS + token exchange path to the private control plane (route: /v1/auth/exchange).
3) Observe the TLS handshake completes but the subsequent identity mapping fails and returns 401.
4) Repeat with a cert where the same identity is present in the SAN (subjectAltName) and the request succeeds consistently.
logs_and_artifacts: Auth-proxy logs show: 'mTLS identity extracted: svc' followed by 'principal lookup failed: svc%20team@corp'. TLS handshake logs show successful handshake. Control-plane RBAC lookup shows a missing key for the decoded form. Packet captures demonstrate that the proxy receives the full CN during handshake but our identity-normalization step truncates at '%'.
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: proxy TLS subject parsing bug where percent sign is treated as delimiter and triggers early truncation.
- Reproduced in staging by mounting a cert with encoded characters; auth-proxy v1.13 exhibits the truncation, while an older sidecar image v1.11 decodes correctly (difference in the OpenSSL wrapper and internal normalization path).
- Root cause narrowed to a new normalization function added in auth-proxy v1.12 that attempted to 'sanitize' subject fields and incorrectly applied percent-decoding only to SAN URIs but not to the CN, then used a split on '%' for legacy reasons. When the decoded value doesn't match RBAC keys (customer uses literal encoded CNs in their IAM system), principal lookups fail.
- Workaround validated: issuing certs that place the identity in the SAN (URI or DNS) or reissuing CNs without percent-encoding removes the failure. Also, temporarily rolling the proxy back to v1.11 in staging restored correct behavior.
customer_communications_summary: 03/10 09:20 - FinServCo opened ticket reporting intermittent 401s after cert rotation. 03/10 11:05 - Support requested sample cert and request id; customer provided for two failing requests. 03/11 14:30 - Engineering confirmed reproducible in staging and supplied workaround (use SAN or reissue without percent-encoding). 03/12 08:15 - Customer applied SAN-based patch; reported reduction in 401s and continues monitoring.
next_steps:
1) Engineering to prepare a patch that removes the fragile '%' split behavior and normalizes CN and SAN consistently (PR linked). Target: auth-proxy v1.13.1.
2) QA to validate against certificates containing reserved characters and run regression tests for subject parsing.
3) Coordinate a controlled rollout to private control planes; include a compatibility flag to opt-in for strict normalization.
4) Customer follow-up: recommend certificate reissue guidance and update IdP automation to avoid percent-encoding in CN when possible.
resolution_notes: Workaround: customer reissued certificates placing principal in SAN; temporary rollback of auth-proxy to v1.11 in one cluster eliminated the errors. Permanent fix pending release of v1.13.1 which will include normalization fix and a migration guide. Post-release, we will coordinate with FinServCo to schedule an upgrade window.
